q-52250.name: Question 2
q-52250.worked_solution:
First, we find the $\text{GCF}$ of the two terms:

$$
\text{GCF}(x(w-6),10(w-6))=w-6
$$

Each term is already written as a product with the $\text{GCF}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (w-6)-10\cdot (w-6)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the $\text{GCF}$ outside the parentheses and keep the remaining terms inside:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (w-6)-10\cdot (w-6) & = \\ (x-10)(w-6) & \end{aligned}
$$

q-52250.html:
Question 2
?

Factor the polynomial expression x(w−6)−10(w−6).

a
10(w−6)
b
(x−6)(w−10)
c
(x−10)(w−6)
d
x(w−6)
e
10x(w−6)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the GCF of the two terms:

GCF(x(w−6),10(w−6))=w−6

Each term is already written as a product with the GCF:

x⋅(w−6)−10⋅(w−6)

Finally, we write the GCF outside the parentheses and keep the remaining terms inside:

x⋅(w−6)−10⋅(w−6)=(x−10)(w−6)

q-52275.html:
Question 3
?

Factor the polynomial expression p(s2−11)−12(s2−11).

a
(p−11)(s2−12)
b
11(p−12)
c
(12−p)(s2−11)
d
(p−12)(s2−11)
e
p(s−11)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the GCF of the two terms:

GCF(p(s2−11),12(s2−11))=s2−11

Each term is already written as a product with the GCF:

p⋅(s2−11)−12⋅(s2−11)

Finally, we write the GCF outside the parentheses and keep the remaining terms inside:

p⋅(s2−11)−12⋅(s2−11)=(p−12)(s2−11)
